analysis.investment_thesis: Prudent is a high-quality financial distributor with exceptional ROCE (44.1%) and 45% net profit CAGR, but the Magic Formula breaks down here on two fronts: it's a financial services company (explicitly excluded from the formula) and the earnings yield of ~2.6% (EBIT INR 292 Cr / EV ~INR 11,409 Cr) is catastrophically below the 12% minimum threshold. Great business, wrong price — the Magic Formula demands both quality AND cheapness, and this stock delivers only one.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROCE of 44.1% and ROE of 34% — sustained over multiple years, indicating genuine competitive advantage in distribution
Net profit CAGR of 45.1% over 6 years with consistent FCF generation (INR 143 Cr in FY25) and near-zero debt (D/E: 0.04)
Asset-light model: minimal capex (~INR 18 Cr) relative to earnings, with operating income growing from INR 40 Cr (2019) to INR 292 Cr (2025)
key_risks: Earnings yield of only 2.6% (EBIT/EV) — the Magic Formula requires >12%; at P/E 53x, the stock prices in flawless execution for many years
Financial services distributor is explicitly excluded from Magic Formula — fee income and AUM-linked revenue distort ROIC calculations
Large negative investing CF (INR -142 Cr in FY25) despite minimal capex suggests heavy investment in financial assets/securities — capital deployment risk if market reverses
red_flags: Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = 292/11,409 = 2.56% — far below the 6% floor, let alone the 12% Magic Formula threshold
Financial services sector: explicitly excluded from Magic Formula — capital structure and revenue recognition distort both metrics
P/B of 14.94x means investors are paying INR 15 for every INR 1 of book value — extreme premium to intrinsic assets
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Prudent: EBIT FY2025 = INR 292 Cr, Enterprise Value = Market Cap (11,397) + Debt (31) - Cash (19) = ~INR 11,409 Cr, giving an Earnings Yield of just 2.56%. This fails spectacularly — I want to see >12%, preferably >15%. ROCE at 44.1% is genuinely excellent and would rank in the top decile of any Magic Formula screen, but the formula requires BOTH legs. One strong leg doesn't make a buy. The business itself is terrific — revenue compounding at 31% annually, profit at 45%, almost no debt, and consistent FCF conversion — but the market knows it too, and has priced it at 53x earnings.

The deeper structural issue: Prudent is a financial services distributor, and Greenblatt explicitly excludes financial companies from Magic Formula because their assets (AUM, trail commissions, financial investments) make ROIC calculations meaningless. The heavy investing outflows (INR -142 Cr in FY25 vs. capex of only INR -18 Cr) suggest substantial deployment into financial assets — confirming this isn't a simple operating business. If you want to own this, you'd need a different framework entirely (perhaps franchise value, AUM growth trajectory). By Magic Formula standards, at 2.56% earnings yield, you're overpaying by roughly 5x what I'd need to get excited.
